data.description:
Context: originally captured 2026-08-03 as "Nothing writes the superseded run D6 promises" — the collision harness (PR #25) found the superseded shape designed for, guarded for, and written by no one, and found D6 clause 2's "stand-down" promise had no mechanism (the loser's daemon notices at renewal, mcp.go renewOnce, and silently untracks). Triaged and grilled 2026-08-04; D6 was rewritten (PR #28 — read the revised D6 clause 3 first, it is the contract). Key recon facts that shaped the design: only the losing agent knows its branch name (daemons learn branches only from finish_run), and a loser that finishes today records a run with outcome done — mislabeled, not lost. This task depends on the confirmation gate (tuh-01KZ5WMT4GWZTYVRGWN4PFN777) and owns the loser's whole story.

The ask:
- Referee every done-recording path: opFinishRun (serving both MCP finish_run and the HTTP run surface) runs the confirmation gate on outcome done. A winning attempt records done. A lost attempt (claim voided, or the contest confirmed for a competitor) is COERCED to outcome superseded — the agent's reported branch/PR/commits/summary are kept as the salvage record — and the tool result says plainly: recorded as superseded, not done; a peer won this task; close any open PR. The MCP surface continues to reject agent-supplied superseded/interrupted (unchanged — the daemon is the referee of how attempts ended; agents report what they did).
- Expiry synthesis for losers that never report: in internal/core/replay.go, a voided claim whose lease has expired with no closing run by that actor gets a synthesized branch-less superseded run — mirror interruptedRun exactly (deterministic: lease data + Now are already replay inputs; synthesized runs already sort after real ones). Pair with the guard change that makes it stable: finishGuardLocked admits a voided claim's close only until that claim's lease expires; after that the attempt is closed forever and a late finish_run is rejected with text pointing at add_note for branch salvage ("your attempt was already closed as superseded; if the branch is worth salvaging, record it with add_note").
- Verb-time stand-down: claim_next/claim_task result text gains the standing warning — before merging anything from this work, call confirm_claim; merging on an unconfirmed claim is a protocol violation (agent-protocol step 5). Any verb a provisionally-voided claimant touches on that task (add_note, escalate, finish_run, release_claim) states the loss plainly in its result. release_claim from a voided claimant currently errors (holderClaimLocked requires the active claim) — make it a clean acknowledged stand-down instead, since standing down is exactly what we asked the loser to do.

Acceptance criteria:
- Core table tests: voided + lease-expired + unclosed → synthesized branch-less superseded run; voided + closed by a real run → no synthesis; the verdict is deterministic at instants before and after expiry; one close per attempt holds.
- Daemon tests: finish_run(done) by a race loser records superseded keeping the reported links, with the stand-down text in the result; finish_run(done) by the confirmed winner records done; a post-synthesis finish is rejected with the add_note pointer; claim responses carry the confirm-before-merge warning; release_claim by a voided claimant succeeds as acknowledgment.
- make test lint green from the repo root.

Constraints: boring Go (T1); replay stays pure; stored bytes never rewritten and the write-side-only guard posture stands (T3 — replay never re-judges stored run.finished events; existing claimless runs on ledgers stand untouched); MCP outcome vocabulary for agents is unchanged; docs/agent-protocol.md as revised in PR #28 is the contract for all result text.
data.title: Loser handling: verb-time stand-down, coerced superseded, expiry synthesis (D6 revision)
